hypothesis: If forced role sharing is associated with unusual rare-token endpoint disagreement, matched input/output alignment and shared-to-matched role distances should be unusually poor in1-9frequency targets. Report every bin and seed; absence of such a pattern weakens this geometric explanation. No geometry outcome can establish a causal gradient mechanism or qualify a new model.
limitations: Within-model role comparisons are endpoint geometry, not gradients or causal errors.
Cross-model coordinates may evolve differently despite shared initialization; cosine distance is not a functional equivalence test.
Input norms are divided by k=1/sqrt192 in both matched and shared models; compare matching roles and report scaling explicitly.
Unweighted vocabulary rows include many tokens never appearing in validation; separate target-weighted summaries prevent silently equating these populations.
Exploratory analysis after overall quality and frequency losses are known; no subgroup hypothesis test or new adoption gate.
scope: Allthree accepted matched/shared H200 pairs; original training-frequency bins; FP64 CPU row norms/angles in1024-row chunks; unweighted vocabulary-type and validation-target-weighted summaries. No model construction, initializer replay, training, inference or new scoring.
